context_rule.plain: Ollama starts with a small memory window: 4k, 32k or 256k tokens, based on your video memory. Coding tools need at least 64k.

runners.name: Ollama
runners.plain: A small background program that downloads models and serves them to other apps on your computer.
runners.how_to_start: Open the Ollama app, or run: ollama serve. Then: ollama pull <model>. For tools that need a big memory window: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve

runners.name: LM Studio
runners.plain: A desktop app to download and chat with models. It can also serve them to other apps.
runners.how_to_start: Open LM Studio, go to the Developer tab and start the server. Or run: lms server start

runners.name: llama.cpp (llama-server)
runners.plain: The engine many other tools are built on. Its server command gives you a web chat and a model URL.
runners.how_to_start: llama-server -m model.gguf -c 32768 --port 8080  (the current README lists 9931 as the default port, older guides say 8080, so set --port yourself)

runners.name: MLX (mlx-lm server)
runners.plain: Apple's engine for Macs with Apple Silicon chips. Its server gives you a model URL.

runners.name: vLLM
runners.plain: A fast model server for computers with a strong Nvidia or AMD graphics card, often shared by a team.

harnesses.name: LM Studio chat
harnesses.plain: A desktop app where you download a model and chat with it. Nothing else to set up.
harnesses.good_for: Easiest private chat on your own computer
harnesses.connect:
Open LM Studio, search for your model in Discover, download it, then open a new chat and pick it.
LM Studio is the runner itself, so there is no URL to enter.

harnesses.name: Jan
harnesses.plain: A free desktop chat app that runs models on your computer. It looks like ChatGPT.
harnesses.good_for: Private ChatGPT-style chat, free and open source
harnesses.connect:
Install Jan, open it, and let it download its first model. Pick any model from the Hub to chat.
Jan has its own built-in engine (llama.cpp), so no URL is needed. It can also serve a model at http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1 for other apps.

harnesses.name: AnythingLLM
harnesses.plain: A desktop app to chat with your own files and documents using a model on your computer.
harnesses.good_for: Asking questions about your own documents
harnesses.connect:
In Settings, choose LLM provider: Ollama. Set the base URL to http://127.0.0.1:11434.
Pick your model in the same screen.

harnesses.name: Msty
harnesses.plain: A desktop chat app with its own local engine. It can reuse models you got with Ollama.
harnesses.good_for: Friendly chat that reuses your Ollama models
harnesses.connect:
Install Msty and download a model inside the app. To reuse Ollama models, follow the how-to page linked as source.
The core desktop app has a free plan.

harnesses.name: Open WebUI
harnesses.plain: A chat website you run yourself. You open it in your browser and talk to your local model.
harnesses.good_for: Team or home chat page with accounts and files
harnesses.install: docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data -e WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
harnesses.connect:
Open http://localhost:3000, then Settings > Admin > Connections. Add the Ollama URL http://host.docker.internal:11434.
For llama.cpp or vLLM, add an OpenAI connection with the URL ending in /v1.
harnesses.license: Open WebUI License (BSD-3 style with a branding rule)

harnesses.name: Continue
harnesses.plain: An add-on for VS Code or JetBrains that chats about your code and edits it for you.
harnesses.good_for: Chat and edits inside your code editor
harnesses.connect:
In your Continue config.yaml add under models: - name: Local, provider: ollama, model: <model-id>
Only add apiBase: http://<host>:11434 if Ollama runs on another machine.

harnesses.name: Cline
harnesses.plain: An editor add-on that plans work, edits files and runs commands. It asks before it acts.
harnesses.good_for: Careful multi-file coding help in your editor
harnesses.connect:
In Cline Settings pick provider Ollama, base URL http://localhost:11434, then pick your model.
Turn on Use Compact Prompt in Settings > Features. A terminal version installs with: npm install -g cline

harnesses.name: Kilo Code
harnesses.plain: A code editor add-on, also with a terminal version, that writes and edits code with a model.
harnesses.good_for: Coding help in VS Code or the terminal
harnesses.connect:
Run ollama serve, then in Kilo Code choose the Ollama provider (not Ollama Cloud) and pick your model, for example ollama/qwen3-coder:30b.
Set Context Window Size (num_ctx) to 32768 or more.

harnesses.name: Zed
harnesses.plain: A fast code editor with a built-in AI helper. It can use a model on your computer.
harnesses.good_for: A modern editor with built-in AI chat and edits
harnesses.connect:
Run ollama pull mistral and keep Ollama running. In Zed, pick an Ollama model in the model menu.
Zed asks Ollama for only 4096 tokens by default. Set language_models.ollama.context_window to 32768 in settings.

harnesses.name: Goose
harnesses.plain: A free helper that codes, runs commands and uses tools. Desktop app and terminal versions exist.
harnesses.good_for: General tasks and coding with tools
harnesses.connect:
Run: goose configure. Choose Configure Providers, then Ollama. Enter the host or leave it empty for localhost:11434.
Use a model with tool calling. Models without it can only chat.

harnesses.name: OpenCode
harnesses.plain: A coding helper that lives in your terminal. It reads your project, edits files and runs commands.
harnesses.good_for: Open source terminal coding agent with many models
harnesses.connect:
Put this in opencode.json: {"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json","provider":{"ollama":{"npm":"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible","name":"Ollama (local)","options":{"baseURL":"http://localhost:11434/v1"},"models":{"<model-id>":{"name":"<model-id>"}}}}}
Or run: ollama launch opencode. Ollama says OpenCode needs 64k context or more.

harnesses.name: Aider
harnesses.plain: A terminal tool where you chat and it edits your code files and saves the changes in git.
harnesses.good_for: Small, safe code edits with git commits
harnesses.connect:
export OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:11434
aider --model ollama_chat/<model>   (Aider sizes the context window for each request itself)

harnesses.name: Qwen Code
harnesses.plain: A terminal coding helper from the Qwen team. It works well with Qwen models and also with others.
harnesses.good_for: Terminal coding agent tuned for Qwen models
harnesses.connect:
Run qwen, then /auth and choose Custom Provider. Or add to ~/.qwen/settings.json under modelProviders.openai: {"id":"<model-id>","name":"<model-id>","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","envKey":"OLLAMA_API_KEY"}
Then set env OLLAMA_API_KEY=ollama (Ollama ignores the key, Qwen Code wants one).

harnesses.name: Codex CLI
harnesses.plain: OpenAI's terminal coding helper. It can also talk to a model on your own computer.
harnesses.good_for: Terminal coding agent with a local model option
harnesses.connect:
Add oss_provider = "ollama" (or "lmstudio") to your Codex config.toml, then run: codex --oss
Or run: ollama launch codex. Ollama says Codex needs a 64k context window.

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.plain: Anthropic's terminal coding helper. Ollama can stand in for the cloud, so a local model does the work.
harnesses.good_for: Terminal coding agent through Ollama's Claude-style endpoint
harnesses.connect:
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 then run: claude --model <model>
Or run: ollama launch claude. Use a model with tool calling and 64k+ context.

harnesses.name: Crush
harnesses.plain: A good-looking terminal coding helper from Charm. It works with many models, local ones included.
harnesses.good_for: Polished terminal coding agent
harnesses.connect:
Add this line to ~/.config/crush/crushrc: provider add ollama --name Ollama --type ollama --base-url "http://localhost:11434/v1/"
Crush then fills in the model list by itself. For llama.cpp use --type llamacpp with your server URL.
harnesses.license: FSL-1.1-MIT (free to use, becomes MIT later)

harnesses.name: Nanocoder
harnesses.plain: A small open source coding helper for the terminal, made by a community group. Local first.
harnesses.good_for: Light local-first terminal coding agent
harnesses.connect:
Run: nanocoder --provider ollama --model <model>
Any OpenAI-compatible URL also works, see the README for the provider setup.

harnesses.name: Pi
harnesses.plain: A tiny terminal coding helper with four basic tools. You add extra features yourself.
harnesses.good_for: Minimal, hackable terminal coding agent
harnesses.connect:
Save as models.json in ~/.pi/agent: {"providers":{"ollama":{"baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","api":"openai-completions","apiKey":"ollama","models":[{"id":"<model-id>"}]}}}
Or run: ollama launch pi

harnesses.name: Hermes Agent
harnesses.plain: A helper from Nous Research that remembers what it learns. It works in the terminal and chat apps.
harnesses.good_for: A long-running agent that learns your habits
harnesses.connect:
Run: hermes model, choose Custom endpoint, enter http://localhost:11434/v1, skip the key, enter your model name.
Hermes refuses to start with less than 64,000 tokens of context. Start Ollama with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000.

harnesses.name: OpenClaw
harnesses.plain: A personal assistant that runs on your computer and answers you in your chat apps.
harnesses.good_for: A private assistant reachable from your phone chats
harnesses.connect:
Run: ollama launch openclaw. By hand, set baseUrl to http://127.0.0.1:11434 with no /v1 at the end.
The /v1 URL breaks tool calling in OpenClaw. Use a 64k+ context window.

harnesses.name: OpenHands
harnesses.plain: A coding helper you open in your browser. It works on tasks in a safe box.
harnesses.good_for: Bigger coding tasks in a browser, in a safe sandbox
harnesses.install: docker run -it --rm --pull=always -e AGENT_SERVER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY=ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server -e AGENT_SERVER_IMAGE_TAG=1.26.0-python -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v ~/.openhands:/.openhands -p 3000:3000 --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway --name openhands-app docker.openhands.dev/openhands/openhands:1.8
harnesses.connect:
Open http://localhost:3000, then LLM Settings > Advanced. Custom Model: openai/<model-id>, Base URL: http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1, API Key: local-llm
That is the LM Studio example. Docs say use at least about 22k tokens of context, 32k or more if you can.
